#1432. 'Managers now are b****y boring!': NEIL WARNOCK on the lack of characters in football, his friendship with Pep Guardiola, why he is open to managing again post-Christmas - and how he almost became a chiropodist!

Published: 19:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 16 November 2026

Spending time in the company of Neil Warnock is always an education, be it witnessing one of his legendary foul-mouthed touchline rants or perched at one of his stage shows at grand venues like London Palladium.

On this occasion, Daily Mail Sport is perched in an east London bar watching on as one of English football's national treasures is posing for some modelling. Yes, you read that right, Mr Warnock is here to launch his own pair of socks with a tipple of Famous Grouse whisky in hand.

The complements on Warnock's 77-year-old feet are soon over, though, and we can get on to talking about a life in football that started six decades ago as a winger for Chesterfield and has traversed 10 clubs as a player, 17 as a manager and more than 2,000 games in the dugout.

So where to start? Maybe his reflections on nearly five decades in management – and how the whole conversation about feet is not too out of place…

'You don't realise how long it has been really, I started off just a team of ragamuffins as I call them,' he says in his iconic Yorkshire accent. 'They used to train on the green where I had digs in Hartlepool and asked me to coach them.

'I remember we scored from a set-piece we worked on, I was running up and down the touchline high-fiving everyone. I got the bug. I knew I could never get to the top as a player, I was quick but I was brainless.

Daily Mail Sport caught up with Neil Warnock to discuss his six decades in football

After representing 10 different clubs as a player, Warnock became one of the most compelling managers in the game

'I could've been a chiropodist if not in football. That could be on a quiz, couldn't it? I had bad feet at Scunthorpe, I used to get massive blisters so the physio there started getting me to do some of the players' feet.

'I enjoyed doing ingrown toenails and things like that! So I thought why not? Then I had a practice in Sheffield. I had to make a decision when we won the league at Scarborough whether to go full-time or pack it in. I thought, "Oh, go on then, let's give it a little go".

'It's not worked out badly, really, has it?

'People come up to me every day and say, "You're a legend, you". And I say, "Oh, thank you very much". Then they tell me what club they support, I have had so many haven't I? Last week I went out for a minute and had four selfies. They all appreciate what I did for their club.

'There aren't as many characters in the game now, you wouldn't get upset with managers now like in my day because now they are that b****y boring! Some of them barely speak.

'They won't get the rapport we had. I managed at a good time. The way I managed, I needed that humour. I needed the lads to enjoy it. I signed a lot of players that many managers wouldn't touch with a barge pole, are you with me? They ended up getting me promotions.'

The aforementioned humour brings us on to a private conversation he had with the great Pep Guardiola, one of the millions of anecdotes up Warnock's sleeve but one that he has not told until now.

'I went to a training session and he asked me to say a few words,' explains Warnock. 'I said, "Well lads I bet you're glad I'm not your manager because we'd be kicking balls from there to there, chasing it, heading it, practicing our tackles"... everyone laughed.

Warnock views Pep Guardiola as the best manager of his lifetime, while the Spaniard praised the veteran's humour after once addressing his Man City squad at a training session

Warnock has led teams to promotions on eight occasions over the course of his career

'After the session we had a coffee and Pep said to me, "Neil, that was amazing, you know when you talked to the players? I understood why you had so many promotions".

'He started counting and said, "What we have is all these staff… computers, details, nutritionist, all these staff, but you know what we don't have? Humour". He noticed why my lads had done well in my teams, just in that meeting. It was good, that. He is amazing.

'Pep is the best manager of my lifetime. They say he had all the best players but it is not easy managing them. Pep did things with players and now there are non-league teams trying to play like Manchester City!'

Warnock is now doing stage tours - Guardiola attended one last season - and had a tear in his eye when he stepped out at London Palladium given he used to watch shows there with his mother, who was in a wheelchair, on the TV as a child.

So what is Warnock up to these days? His current role is advisor at Torquay United but last management job was at Aberdeen two years ago… so is he out of the rat race for good this time?

'No, not really, no,' he says. 'I only work from February to April! So the phone will be on after Christmas. You never know, do ya? There will be someone thinking "why don't we get that Warnock in?".

'I've retired 40 times! Every time I have said it, I have meant it. But it's that dressing room camaraderie. There's something about football, when I look at some of the managers now… they just don't excite me.

'I remember Ruben Amorim (breaks down laughing). He's got his computer out on the bench! I remember watching and thinking, "I'm sorry, son, you need more than a computer to help you tonight!".

Warnock is currently doing stage tours, with Guardiola among the attendees last season

Warnock's current role is advisor at Torquay United and briefly served as interim manager last season, with the 77-year-old admitting he had not completely ruled out a return to the dugout

'And likewise, I see them making notes on the bench, oh my god. I think "what are you doing, your shopping list for Tescos?".

'I do enjoy walking and I enjoy photography, believe it or not. I go up the river with my phone, there's so many lovely things to see.

'I've got an electric bike and I sometimes do about 25 miles. I was thinking of doing a cycle of all my clubs but that would take me five years! They go at about 30mph down the hills, you've got to be careful, you wouldn't want to come off them.'

He is also enjoying fishing, being with the family and playing golf with his son, a PGA rising star William - though Warnock Sr insists he often embarrasses himself playing off 'the ladies' tee'.

The thing that makes Warnock most proud is the four promotions at Wembley but also the togetherness he fostered in his many teams.

He tells us: 'What I like about the teams I had, they all have reunions. You look at the tele now, someone will score a goal and kiss the badge… they won't have a reunion.

'When I go to these reunions, I see all my lads and how I blended that dressing room together and I look at the comradeship they still have now, they are the same as they were just a lot older.

'This year, my Scarborough team are having a 40-year celebration and the lads have invited me. I said there's no way I'm going out with that lot after the do because they can drink, let me tell you!'

#1431. Biotech innovations are an opportunity to limit climate change

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Climate change is affecting many types of crop, including these unusually small potatoes.Credit: John Thys/AFP/Getty

Policymakers at the United Nations COP31 climate conference that started this week in Antalya, Turkey, will know that the UN Environment Programme has confirmed that global warming will exceed the limit of 1.5 °C above pre-industrial temperatures agreed in 2015 in Paris. This meeting comes hot on the heels of the UN COP17 biodiversity summit in Yerevan, Armenia, which affirmed yet again that the world is also in the middle of a biodiversity crisis. Progress in each case, whether preventing dangerous climate change or stemming biodiversity loss, is too slow. But researchers across scientific disciplines are now arguing that advances in biotechnology could provide solutions1. Methods such as gene editing and germplasm mining — the analysis of huge libraries of plant-genome sequences to find useful traits for crop improvement — can now be used to tackle global warming and protect nature, scientists write in a climate-themed issue of Nature Biotechnology.

There was a time — not that long ago — when many considered biotechnologies a threat to the environment. But as the special issue shows, a shift is under way. Now, the field offers strategies for protecting both climate and biodiversity from the many damaging effects of industrial agriculture.

To feed a growing global population, between 2015 and 2024, the amount of cultivated land grew by roughly eight million hectares a year1. Yet, if the greenhouse-gas emissions, and thus global warming, this expansion causes is to be avoided, the world must work out how to produce enough food within its current agricultural footprint. Land clearance and land-use change contributes up to five billion tonnes of carbon annually — and is a major cause of biodiversity loss. Here, biotech solutions have some of the greatest potential, for example, by helping to increase crop yields and to protect plants from heat, drought and disease.

How biotechnology can mitigate climate change by curbing the global land squeeze

How biotechnology can mitigate climate change by curbing the global land squeeze

Of 77 such technologies with applications in agriculture, aquaculture and other sectors, many are ready for large-scale testing in the field, propose bioengineers Shekhar Mishra, Lauren Lui and Adam Arkin at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory in California in a Perspective article2. Argentina, China and the United States have given the green light to engineered drought-tolerant crops.

Rice farming produces around 9% of human-caused emissions of the greenhouse gas methane. Now, researchers have found a way to slash these emissions, write agronomist Yunkai Jin at Hunan Agricultural University in Changsha, China, and his colleagues in a Comment article3.

But technological readiness isn’t enough: governments, regulators and the public need to be ready, too4. Readers might have a sense of déjà vu: in the 1990s, advances in biotechnology promised a revolution in food and agriculture — which subsequently stalled. The ambition was to genetically modify crops or engineer them in other ways so that they could tolerate herbicides, resist insects and fight viruses. But, at the time, many scientists, governments and corporations promoting the technology gave insufficient attention to several issues.

Deployability of biotechnologies for environmentally resilient agriculture

Deployability of biotechnologies for environmentally resilient agriculture

One concern was public anxiety about the idea of eating food produced using transgenic technologies — crops modified by inserting a gene from another plant species or other organism. Another issue was that risks to the environment and to human health had not been studied sufficiently. A third problem was that multinational companies dominated both the research and the development of these technologies, creating fears that the rise of agricultural biotechnology would put many small family farms out of business.

Environmental groups found common cause with consumer organizations. Together, they urged governments to enact strict regulations. In the European Union, for example, risks to human health and the environment needed to be assessed before technologies producing genetically modified organisms could be commercialized. Although this was necessary, it slowed down advances in low- and middle-income countries, because any nation intending to export produce to the EU would have to prove that it was not genetically modified.

Since then, at least two things have changed, increasing optimism about the use of biotechnology to help the planet. The discovery of gene editing — in which an organism’s genes are modified precisely to produce specific traits — has proved transformational for agriculture. The method is being developed cautiously and is regulated in a more nuanced way than were conventional technologies that produce genetically modified crops. In June, the EU amended its regulations on genetic modification and now permits the cultivation of some gene-edited crops.

Low-methane rice is near — the world should deploy it

Low-methane rice is near — the world should deploy it

A second development is that catastrophic events such as heatwaves and floods have meant that climate change and the planet’s protection have become mainstream concerns across science and society, not just for environmental research. In a way, we all need to be environmentalists now, and this provides a rationale for governments to reconsider adopting biotech solutions with appropriate safeguards in place.

Advances in biotechnology that limit land use should be deployed to slow down the rise in global temperatures and biodiversity loss. This will require a partnership between the private sector, scientists, conservationists and farmers. High-yielding crops produced using industrial agriculture have helped to feed the world but have also had a devastating effect on biodiversity. Organic agriculture is more sustainable but requires extra land, because its yields tend to be lower than those from industrial methods. Providing they are implemented wisely, safely and ethically, biotechnologies could contribute to innovative farming methods that offer the best of both worlds.

#1430. England's evolution: James Trafford and two other stars chisel their names into the XI, Thomas Tuchel learning from Argentina and Jude Bellingham playing like a captain!

Published: 02:32 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:25 EST, 16 November 2026

England ended world champions Spain's 43-match unbeaten run in dramatic fashion with a 3-2 win on a memorable night in Madrid.

After Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored to establish a three-goal lead, the visitors had to cling on after Elliot Anderson was sent off and the hosts scored twice in the final half hour.

The victory means Thomas Tuchel's side top their Nations League group and it provided a strong riposte to criticism of the manager following the World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was at the Metropolitano Stadium, and here are his FIVE big take-aways…

It would not have mattered had England conceded a late equaliser. To draw comparison with Argentina in the final half hour is unfair and inaccurate. The World Cup semi-final was 11v11 and so, when we draw conclusions from this game, let us do so on the same terms.

Thomas Tuchel was delighted with his England players as they won 3-2 away in Spain

And what did England do at 11v11 with a 1-0 lead? They attacked. And attacked again. This was a major change (and improvement) and is the reason for such encouragement. They have learnt from a mistake, as much as Tuchel will be loathe to admit.

Mexico would be a fairer parallel, but that was against opposition far inferior to Spain. At 11v10, we could not expect England to stay on the front foot here, as they were until the point of Jarell Quansah's needless mistake and Elliot Anderson's subsequent red card.

And that is cause for great optimism - because this game was not in the balance in any way when the teams were at equal number.

For me, and I don't think this is even close, this was the best performance of Tuchel's reign.

Do England suddenly have a pair of full backs?! After years of trawling and trialling, here in the most testing of surrounds, Ben White and Lewis Hall inked their names into Tuchel's XI.

We can forgive the concession of two goals when down to 10 men - because with 11, Spain barely looked like getting a shot on target. In fact, they didn't.

Much of that was down to the solidity of the full backs. Then, with backs to the wall, the pair became bricks in the resistance. One White block late on was heroic.

Before that, Hall's best work was not in containing Lamine Yamal, but in emulating him. His dribbles were daring and unnerved Spain, who thought they would spend the game in England's half and with the ball. They did neither early on and Hall was central to that.

White's goal had shades of Carlos Alberto on the overlap, and his England redemption arc felt like it reached completion here. Let him now move on now, for England need him.

No more boos, please, only cheers for White (and Hall).

It's time to stop the boos for Ben White after he starred with Lewis Hall at full back

Ezri Konsa is England's best defender. Build the backline around him.

Tuchel said on the eve of the game that he thought Konsa had grown for the move to Arsenal, and this was proof.

Boy do England need a mature, reliable presence at the heart of their defence. Konsa showed here why he can be that man. He scored a fine goal, which is always a sign of a defender ready to take wider responsibility, but it was his cool interceptions and desperate blocks at the other end that were most reassuring.

What Konsa has to do now is build on this - and a man-of-the-match performance at the home of the world champions is a pretty lofty and solid foundation from which to do so.

Tuchel will, and should, be giving serious thought to keeping James Trafford in England's goal for the Nations League quarter-finals.

Jordan Pickford has done nothing wrong. And yet, it feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and here was his justification.

Trafford can be a little erratic and immature. What better way to grow, emotionally, than with a series of saves to preserve an historic win. He will feel like a different player, and person, to the one who started this game. Like White and Hall, this felt like a coming-of-age night in an England jersey.

Trafford has all the tools. He might just have used them to chisel his name into that team-sheet.

Goalkeeper feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and James Trafford starred

Spain's fans are left shocked as Ezri Konsa hails the brilliant Trafford in emphatic fashion

No goals, but England would not have won this game without Bellingham. He terrified Spain, perhaps given their intimate knowledge of his brilliance.

Beating the best is as much a mental challenge as it is physical, and Bellingham believed. He made England believe, too.

His swagger. His majesty. And yes, his skill. Of all the positives from this win, it is hard to look past Bellingham as the biggest reason for England being able to challenge Spain at the top of the world rankings.

Jude Bellingham played like a captain, dropping into midfield when down to 10 men

He won the corner for the second goal and created the third. He then dropped into midfield when down to 10 and played like a captain.

That is what England need - Bellingham the leader, not Bellingham the individual. He has bought into the collective under Tuchel and, with that, his team-mates are buying into his big ideas. They don't come much bigger than what England achieved here.

Right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

#1427. How Vinicius Jr's lavish summer holiday has left him playing catch up: Real Madrid star admits he 'trained less' while on luxury yacht trip and blames Brazil's early World Cup exit - and 'overwhelming' Arsenal rumours - for sluggish start to the season

Published: 09:07 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:48 EST, 16 November 2026

Vinicius Junior has admitted his lavish summer holiday after Brazil's last-16 World Cup exit is behind his slow start with Real Madrid this season.

And the winger says he felt 'overwhelmed' by the interest of clubs such as Arsenal  and insecurity around his contract renewal talks in Madrid.

He has scored one goal and provided three assists in 12 games this season, and amid the criticism, manager Jose Mourinho has even said he should have left this summer to go somewhere he is 'respected'.

Vini Jr said: 'I don’t think I prepared better after the World Cup because the impact of this tournament is very significant for all Brazilians. Losing so early was something we didn’t expect.

'So I took advantage of the holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in recent years. This may have affected my start to the season.

'Also, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs interested last summer, I felt really overwhelmed, as did the situation at Real Madrid. But the season is very long.

Vinicius Junior has admitted his lavish summer holiday is behind his slow start to the season (Instagram: vinijr)

The Real Madrid star spent plenty of time relaxing on yachts as he visited Brazil, Jamaica, Italy, and Dubai (Instagram: vinijr)

The 26-year-old got around via private jet and said that he wants to 'enjoy life' (Instagram: vinijr)

'Maintaining such a high level for so long is always very difficult. I believe only Cristiano Ronaldo and (Lionel) Messi have managed to maintain it for so many years, achieving the same numbers.

'I'm human, I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve. I try to understand more about football, about the day-to-day, but I'm 26 years old and I have to enjoy life a little too.

'Last season, until December, I had only scored five goals. Then, I finished with more than 20 goals, as in all other seasons. I believe I am preparing, evolving, because, in the most decisive moment of the season, I am always there.'

Vini Jr spent part of his summer break in his home city of Sao Goncalo, as well as visiting Jamaica, Italy, and Dubai.

His Instagram was full of pictures of him relaxing on yachts, speeding around on a private jet, and showing off his fashionable outfits.

Arsenal enquired about the Brazilian superstar and reports suggested they were willing to offer him a mammoth £18.5million per season - more than any player at the club.

His contract expires at the end of the season and the club's position is that he must lower his demands if they are to agree an extension. They would still be willing to make him their joint-highest earner alongside Kylian Mbappe.

He has often been a target of racism in Spain - there have been more than 20 such cases of alleged abuse towards him since he joined from Flamengo in 2018. The situation has reduced him to tears before, but he has insisted on staying in La Liga so that he doesn't 'give the racists what they want'.

The winger - who has scored one goal and provided three assists this season - was a target for Arsenal and could leave Madrid in January

The winger is currently serving a four-match ban for pulling Villarreal star Nathan Saliba's hair.

And Mourinho said last month: 'If I were in his shoes, I probably wouldn't be here. I would have forced a move to a country where he'd be respected, but out of loyalty to Real Madrid and love for the club, he stayed.

'He believes things can improve, and he still has that smile. Nothing and no one can take it away from him.

'He's a fantastic guy, and it's easy to get along with him. I spend a few minutes alone with him every day.

'I value him immensely because he always manages to live and survive with a smile.'

Vinicius has been a phenomenon at Real Madrid, scoring 129 times in 388 games from the wing.

But the balance of power shifted to Mbappe when he joined from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024 and talk of his future has increased.

There is a chance that, if Madrid go a third season in a row without significant silverware, they choose to rebuild and go in a different direction.

Moving away from the heavy 'superstar' model has worked for PSG and rewarded them with two Champions League titles in a row.

Vinicius had a tricky summer, being knocked out of the last 16 of the World Cup with Brazil and then missing his pre-season return date as his representatives tried to revive talks over a contract extension.

If an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Madrid could be open to selling in January, rather than lose him for free next summer.

Last year Al Ahli were willing to offer a €1bn five-year contract offer for the 2024 Ballon d'Or runner-up.

Liverpool were also credited with interest earlier this window but are not in the mix for a player who earns around £520,000 a week.

#1426. Romelu Lukaku announces 'bombshell' international retirement: Former Chelsea star, 33, U-turns on his Belgium future - leaving Belgian press stunned

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 08:03 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:49 EST, 16 November 2026

Romelu Lukaku has announced his retirement from international football in a 'bombshell' decision that has left the Belgian press utterly stunned.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United forward, 33, vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team, although he now appears to have changed his mind over his future.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku took to social media on Monday morning to break the unexpected news.

'16 years old,' his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'

Belgium legend Romelu Lukaku has announced his decision to retire from international football

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking on the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retires as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

Belgian newspapers were caught out by the shock announcement, which was described as an 'unexpected bombshell' by outlet HLN on Monday.

Lukaku's stock within the international set-up has fallen since he promised the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament in January.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the tournament under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1

Axel Witsel sent a heartfelt message to Lukaku on Instagram: 'Thanks for everything, legend'

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute - and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he said.

'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.

No. Ask about their breathing requirements. Then say, “Oh, sorry, we don’t breathe that,” and change the subject immediately. Do not revisit the topic.

They are always the last of their kind. The last of its kind has a lot of free time and a lot of anger. Do not become its hobby.

You will. Internalize it. You have practice. Panic is normal. Displaying it is optional and discouraged. Don’t be a target.

You are still breathing and they do not know where the rest of us are. That is considered a success under current guidelines. Survival is the only metric.

#1423. Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager said. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw

It had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick said: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”

When asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

3 - Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? https://t.co/DuSpvymZfu

The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

“We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

“We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”

More jeers at the final whistle from United fans - they weren’t happy with this point against a team there for the taking after Rodrigo Bentancur’s dismissal. Michael Carrick is still trying to find answers because this United team is not clicking.

The late chaos is over at Old Trafford as Solanke rescues a precious point for Tottenham with that 92nd minute equaliser. Man Utd thought they had the game wrapped up after Mbeumo’s well-taken opener was followed by Bentancur’s crazy red card. However, Spurs, who were the better team throughout the contest, kept fighting and found a fully deserved leveller. The visitors remain winless, but it’s another worrying performance from Carrick’s side, who have picked up just one victory in six top-flight matches.

A point apiece in Manchester. https://t.co/xiEiQsFsje

Dalot and Gray are both handed yellow cards for fouls that broke up play. Despite their numerical disadvantage, Spurs currently look like the more likely side to claim a victory.

It’s just the Spurs fans singing in Old Trafford now. They fully deserved that equaliser. Rashford and Heaven are on for the hosts, with Cunha and Shaw taken off.

Incredible drama at Old Trafford! Tonali floats a cross into the box and Solanke shrugs off Martinez, before flicking a delicate header into the bottom corner to send Spurs’ away support wild. Man Utd are stunned. Could the visitors go on and win this now?

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw

Van Hecke does well to block Cunha’s effort and the referee indicates that there will be a minimum of eight minutes of added time.

De Zerbi’s final roll of the dice in search of a late leveller sees Fernandes replace Senesi for the remaining few minutes. Spurs must throw everyone forward now.

Martinez lunges in on Maddison and brings down the playmaker with a foul. The centre-back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Baleba unleashes Mbeumo with an over-the-top through ball. Racing through on goal, the forward shoots, but from an unfavourable angle, Kinsky parries his near post effort out for a corner.

Fernandes is cautioned after catching Van Hecke with a late challenge on his ankle. Spurs players aren’t happy with the tackle.

Bentancur’s recklessness has left Spurs with a mountain to climb. Their chance of a comeback looks a bit slimmer now that Man Utd have a numerical advantage on the pitch.

It’s all kicked off at Old Trafford! Bentancur flies in with a risky challenge on Shaw. The Man Utd defender is furious with the tackle and the two players square up to each other. Shaw pushes Bentancur over and the midfielder responds by leaning into the Englishman, creating a headbutt-like action. Shaw and Van Hecke are also given yellows for their roles in that altercation.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc

Rodrigo Bentancur is sent off... and here's why ⬇️ https://t.co/3ahzz5iUbg

Spurs respond to going behind by making a double change as Van de Ven and Maddison come on to replace Udogie and Gallagher.

It’s against the run of play, but Man Utd won’t care, they have the all-important advantage! Cunha runs into a channel and slips a pass into Mbeumo. Van Hecke allows the forward to turn and Mbeumo slides a delightful effort into the far bottom corner. Old Trafford erupts in joy. Tottenham can’t believe it.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe

Tonali’s pass is intercepted by Maguire, but the ball trickles into the onrushing Savio’s path. The winger’s powerful first-time effort is blocked by Mainoo’s sliding challenge and flies over the bar.

It’s Tottenham’s turn to make some alterations as Bentancur and Marmoush enter the action, replacing Bergvall and Kudus.

Zirkzee turns Senesi and threads a pass through to Fernandes. From a tight angle, the Man Utd captain slices a ferocious effort into the side netting. The playmaker has been quiet today, but you can never write him off from scoring or providing an assist.

Baleba’s first action in a Man Utd shirt sees the midfielder smash a hopeful volley wildly off target. Can Baleba’s introductrion lift the crowd and help give the hosts some impetus?

Carrick has seen enough, ordering a much-needed triple change. Baleba replaces Tielemans to make his Man Utd debut. The other changes see Amad and Yoro withdrawn for Zirkzee and Dalot.

🔛 Here comes Carlos! 🇨🇲 Our no.20 makes his United debut as part of a triple change... https://t.co/jGEL8ui0PI

Van Hecke wins the header at the back post of a corner, looping the ball right back into the danger zone, but Maguire is there to crucially nod it over the bar.

Man Utd have the ball in the net, but it won’t count, as Cunha failed to keep it in play before teeing up Tielemans to finish from close range. Old Trafford thought it had lift-off against the run of play, but they’ve been denied by the correct decision.

Tottenham will be kicking themselves! Once again, Savio is causing trouble for Man Utd, driving at the home side’s defence before crossing for Solanke. The striker beats Martinez to the delivery, but directs his half-volley over the bar. That is another hugely frustrating passage of play for Spurs, and yet another missed opportunity. De Zerbi can’t believe it.

How have Tottenham not scored there?! Savio races through after latching onto Tonali’s piercing pass. Maguire can’t keep up with the winger’s pace as he reaches the byline. Kudus and Solanke are waiting for a tap-in inside the six-yard box, but the ball lands at Shaw’s feet, and he clears.

A promising spell of Man Utd pressure ends with Van Hecke stretching to clear Shaw’s searching delivery out for a corner.

We are back under way for the second half at Old Trafford. Both sides are unchanged at the break.

That’s the question De Zerbi will be asking himself and his players at half-time...

Boos greet the half-time whistle as Man Utd have underperformed on their return to Premier League action. However, luckily for the hosts, Tottenham have lacked composure in front of goal, with Solanke, Kudus and Gallagher all missing notable chances.

Nothing to separate @ManUtd and @SpursOfficial at half-time... https://t.co/yJc8pvyfLl

There will be one minute of added time to round off this first half.

Spurs go close again! Solanke plays in Gallagher, who bundles his way into the six-yard box. Tielemans, Martinez and Yoro all fail to apprehend the Spurs midfielder, who digs a close-range shot out of his feet. However, Lammens is there to make a crucial block and thwart the visitors.

Spurs have been on top in this half but there has been a lack of quality from both teams. It has been a scrap between two average teams. Conor Gallagher the most influential player on the pitch so far.

Following Solanke and Kudus’ earlier chances, Spurs have been quiet going forward. Man Utd have been slowly growing into the game.

Amad is dribbling with intent and Gallagher bumps into him. The referee doesn’t give a free-kick and the home fans aren’t happy with that decision. It’s also worth remembering that Gallagher is on a yellow card. He needs to be careful.

Amad forces a save from Kinsky! Man Utd clear a Tottenham corner and burst forward on the counter through Mbeumo. The former Brentford man is chased by Tonali and has Amad in support, before playing the pass into the 24-year-old. Udogie closes down the angle, forcing Amad to take the chance with a first-time shot. His fizzing strike is comfortably collected by Kinsky, but that is more encouraging from the hosts.

You can feel the nervousness in the Old Trafford crowd. Spurs’ dominance has calmed over the last 10 minutes, but Man Utd have failed to take control or pick up the tempo.

This game looks it could be time for Baleba’s much-anticipated debut. Man Utd’s current midfield doesn’t possess enough running power and Tottenham are exploiting that.

Man Utd’s slow start prompts some boos from the home fans. Cunha attempts to rally the crowd, but his side have given their supporters nothing to be positive about in this game so far. From a Spurs perspective, you can see why they’ve only scored two top-flights goals this season. They should be two-nil up, but they’ve notably lacked end-product.

Tottenham miss another golden chance! It’s a brilliant passing move from defence to attack. It ends with Savio teeing up Kudus with an intelligent cross. The Ghanaian can’t quite fully wrap his foot around the delivery, and from inside the penalty area, he slams an unmarked effort wide of the bottom corner.

Currently, Man Utd are being outnumbered in midfield. The interchangeability of Tonali, Bergvall and Gallagher is running rings around Mainoo and Tielemans. Fernandes’ lack of defensive instinct is leaving the hosts’ midfield pivot exposed.

Man Utd then make a rare foray forward as Cunha whips in a cross towards Amad. Udogie is alert to the danger and gets in front of the winger to clear.

Ex-Nottingham Forest manager Steve Cooper is here in the directors’ box at Old Trafford. He was last at Brondby in Denmark and will inevitably be considered for jobs here in England as chairmen look to make changes during the season.

Still, it’s Tottenham forcing the issue as Kudus dashes past Shaw with his blistering pace. Cunha tracks back but can’t stop the winger from digging out a cross. Yoro’s skewed clearance is headed back to Lammens by Tielemans. Man Utd need to careful, they cannot continue playing like this.

The visitors then steam forward again on the counter. On this occasion, Yoro defends magnificently, executing a well-timed sliding tackle on Van Hecke.

The visitors have made an excellent start to this game. Savio breezes past Maguire like he isn’t even there, but can’t quite find Kudus with his low cross. De Zerbi will want his side to capitalise on this dominant period. Man Utd look sluggish and asleep so far.

Gallagher receives an early yellow card after pulling Maguire back. Referee Attwell isn’t taking any prisoners. Man Utd supporters also show their love and appreciation for Rui Pinto with this banner.

Tottenham waste a huge chance! What is Lammens doing?! The Man Utd goalkeeper tries to pick out Mainoo with a very risky pass. It’s intercepted by Bergvall, who tees up Solanke. One-on-one with Lammens, the Spurs striker’s whipped effort is blocked by Lammens. The Belgian goes from zero to hero, emphatically redeeming himself.

We are under way at Old Trafford. Can either of these sides pick up a victory to relieve the pressure on their head coach?

“You cheating b******s, you know what you are,” is heard from the stands at Old Trafford. It’s pretty safe to say they are referring to Manchester City’s guilty verdict which was announced during the international break.

Man Utd, skippered by Fernandes, receive a feverish reception as they’re welcomed onto the pitch by the Old Trafford faithful. Tottenham are led out by Solanke, who captains the visitors today.

With kick-off fast approaching, here’s a recap of both line-ups.

Man Utd: Lammens, Yoro, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw, Tielemans, Mainoo, Diallo, Fernandes, Mbeumo, Cunha.

Our Spurs side to face Man Utd 🫡 🔢 @krakenfx https://t.co/jZOhKEUoYc

Michael Carrick has made two changes to the side which drew against Fulham. Amad Diallo returns to the fold after a spell on the sidelines with an injury, replacing Marcus Rashford, who drops to the bench. The other alteration comes in defence, with Diogo Dalot departing for Leny Yoro.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Manchester United and Tottenham at Old Trafford.

If Manchester City had not entered a legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching 114 charges relating to financial regulations by an independent panel, then surely there would be more pressure on the two head coaches in the dugout this evening?

Man Utd and Tottenham have undoubtedly both endured extremely disappointing starts to their respective top-flight campaigns. The hosts sit just inside the bottom half of the table after picking up just five points from their opening five matches. It’s going even worse for Tottenham, who languish in 20th with zero wins and just two points.

The perilous landscape leaves only one reasonable conclusion: this has all the ingredients for an early season six-pointer.

The strain is perhaps less intense on Michael Carrick, with the Englishman having built up a bundle of goodwill after cleaning up the mess left by Ruben Amorim last season as Man Utd eventually finished third, qualifying for the Champions League. Fans were left slightly underwhelmed by the club’s transfer window, with the players at Carrick’s disposal having not forged any momentum so far in this campaign.

The spotlight is definitely shining more intensely upon Roberto De Zerbi after big-spending Tottenham splashed over £300m in the summer on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Savio. However, the Italian boss is yet to strike the correct rhythm with his newly-formed squad. An encouraging performance backed up by a positive result here at Old Trafford could be the perfect antidote to ease the worries of fans fearing that Tottenham could be embroiled in another relegation battle.

All eyes are on this one. Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1422. Klopp breaks ranks to savage Infantino: Liverpool legend becomes first boss to turn on FIFA president - who is WORSE than Sepp Blatter - as pressure mounts after World Cup farce

Published: 08:02 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 10:36 EST, 16 November 2026

Jurgen Klopp has called on FIFA's embattled president Gianni Infantino to resign, becoming the first national team manager to do so.

Infantino's reputation took a nosedive after his sycophantic behaviour towards Donald Trump before and during the World Cup - most memorably by awarding him a 'FIFA Peace Prize'.

And it only got worse when his clandestine plot to sell off stakes in the World Cup, a devious scheme which would have banked him millions, was revealed by The Times.

Now Germany manager Klopp has hit out: 'There is now a unanimous consensus that a change would make sense.

'I thought that, after Sepp Blatter, the situation couldn't get any worse - but here we are.

'Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.

Jurgen Klopp has publicly savaged FIFA president Gianni Infantino, becoming the first national team manager to do so

The Germany manager said Infantino - who tried to sell off stakes in the World Cup to his own benefit - is 'worse' than his predecessor Sepp Blatter

'Without a doubt, there are people who truly care about football and have no financial interests,' the former Liverpool manager said.

Infantino has clung on to his job thus far, surviving a crisis summit in Morocco in August, despite intense and widespread opposition.

A total of 90 nations including all of UEFA's teams rebelled, with threats to boycott FIFA competitions, and Infantino's £3.1billion plan fell apart.

But he still maintained a large swell of support among Africa, Asia, and South America - especially after offering each nation £30million if they supported his plan. His opponents pointed out that he could simply have given money from FIFA's cash reserves of roughly £4.5b.

In the pages of this historic newspaper, football legend Luis Figo wrote that 'Infantino must go' and accused him of 'debasing the office of FIFA President'.

FIFA does not have a history of picking good leaders - Blatter resigned in 2015 amid allegations of corruption, though he was cleared alongside Michel Platini last year.

Infantino now looks well-placed to be re-elected for a fourth term in next March's presidential elections.

The deadline for candidacies to be submitted is November 18.

Philippe Diallo, the French Football Federation president, has agreed to run against Infantino and has the backing of UEFA's executive committee.

'(Diallo has) extensive experience across all levels of the game, having led the organisation representing French professional football clubs, served on the board of the French professional league and within FIFA’s dispute resolution structures, before becoming President of the FFF and a member of the UEFA Executive Committee in 2023,' UEFA said.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has already announced his intention to be a rival to Infantino.

Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association, is also reportedly set to mount a challenge.

Ex-Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger was touted as a potential challenger but it is understood he told European football’s governing body UEFA that he would not stand.

#1421. Pressing with intensity, getting runners beyond Kane and playing like a 'Premier League team': How Thomas Tuchel's new-look England dismantled Spain - and what he's learned from cowardly retreat against Argentina

Published: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026

By the end of the World Cup, it felt as if Argentina had ripped the mask off Thomas Tuchel’s England only to reveal Gareth Southgate’s England standing there blinking right back at them.

On the biggest stage, against the biggest teams, under the biggest pressure, England wilted as they always did. They sat back, they were too cautious, and they lost. And yet, ever since, Tuchel has turned England into a free-scoring winning machine, topped off by a famous victory in Madrid, ending Spain’s 43-match unbeaten streak.

In the six games since the summer, England have scored 19 goals and conceded six. Five of those have been against the world champions.

Yes, this was the Nations League and not a World Cup semi-final. No, it wasn’t at the end of a gruelling five weeks of heat, humidity and altitude. And, yes, it was only a terrific late double save from James Trafford that stopped this being yet another tale of self-sabotaging England, thanks to Elliot Anderson’s red card, blowing another lead when under pressure.

But, this time, England did see it out. They secured Tuchel’s biggest win as England boss and, in doing so, showed us just how he’s been able to get his side playing his way.

Harry Kane leads the England celebrations after his side's victory over Spain in Madrid on Sunday night

Remember when everyone used to lose their minds whenever Harry Kane dropped deep in big games under Southgate? He’s our bloody striker, for goodness sake. Get in the box!

After England’s defeat by Spain in the Euro 2024 final two years ago, Opta posted on X that Kane had touched the ball just once in the opposition box across both that game and their previous final heartbreak against Italy three years earlier.

‘One fewer than Jack Grealish,’ the post continued. ‘Grealish played 21 minutes in the 2020 final and didn't make the Euro 2024 squad.’

Ballon d’Or winner Kane has made it quite clear since that he doesn’t need to spend all his time in the box to influence games. When he drops deeper, Kane is able to show the full extent of his creativity and range of passing.

The main problem with the ploy under Southgate, however, was that Kane rarely had the team-mates to make the right runs ahead of him. He was surrounded by players who wanted to take up similar positions. Just look at the average position maps (below) from England’s loss to Spain at Euro 2024 compared to last night.

The average position map of England’s players in the loss to Spain at Euro 2024 show how Kane dropped deep, without team-mates making runs for him to exploit

...whereas on Sunday night he had runners - Anthony Gordon, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers - around and beyond him

Two years ago, the only player who averaged their touches ahead of Kane was Bukayo Saka. Jude Bellingham was out wide. Kobbie Mainoo and Phil Foden were basically in Kane’s shadow.

On Sunday night, he had Anthony Gordon, the brilliant, belligerent Bellingham and Morgan Rogers all ahead of him – and nearly even Ben White.

That desire, and instruction, to flock forward under Tuchel has made such a difference.

Take England’s third goal (below). Kane has the ball outside the area. Rogers is bombing on to his left. Gordon, who started as a winger but finds himself occupying the central spaces Kane leaves behind, darts into the box and points to where he wants it.

Bellingham is demanding the ball, too, showing Kane he wants it to feet. Even Anderson is charging into the box. Kane finds Bellingham, who feeds the unseen White, sprinting forward on the overlap to finish.

Kane picks up the ball and is met with an array of options in front of him, ahead of England's third goal

He did similar in the win against Croatia a few days earlier, too.

Kane collects the ball deep with four bodies ahead of him, including full backs Lewis Hall and Trent Alexander-Arnold.

It his raking pass to the back post which allows Bellingham to set up Rogers to finish.

Kane's lofted pass to Rogers (top right) leads to a goal against Croatia for Bellingham (edge of box)

England’s fluidity in the final third is bamboozling defences. That is how you get the best of Kane’s creativity.

Football is changing, so Pep Guardiola told us all in January last year. The modern game is now how teams like Bournemouth and Brighton play. The current Premier League table would suggest he had a point.

Over the past few years in the English top flight, we have seen teams move away from an obsession with keeping the ball for the sake of it and turn towards a far faster, more aggressive and more physical style of play.

Tuchel wants to take from that playbook. ‘We're at our best when we're free, physically overpowering and making it Premier League-level,’ said Kane after last month's 7-0 rout of Croatia.

In the six matches since the World Cup, Tuchel’s England are having much less of the ball than they did at the start of his reign – and now less even than under Southgate.

The key is they are becoming ever more direct with it. Tuchel wants his England to play out of the back with short passes, entice opponents on to them, but then move it through the lines at speed.

Since the World Cup, England are playing far fewer passes, but more of them into the box – to find those runners. A higher percentage of them forward. More direct attacks, moving the ball up the field at a quicker speed.

On Sunday night, they showed how Tuchel wants his side to press. ‘We were hungry in the opposition half,’ said the England boss at full time.

A fine example of that (below) came just after just six minutes. Declan Rice gives his Arsenal team-mate Martín Zubimendi no time at all on the ball inside his own area, charging him down, and forcing him to play out to another Gunner in Mikel Merino. But he, too, is being harassed by Anderson and eventually England win it back and set up Kane for a chance that he fizzes wide.

A half-fit Rice was unable to apply that pressure in the summer.

Declan Rice charges forward to close down Martin Zubimendi who has possession just inside the Spanish box with Kane and Bellingham already engaged in a high press...

...Zubimendi passes to Mikel Merino but Elliot Anderson is all over him and it leads to Kane shot that just fizzes wide

So much of this improvement under Tuchel into a side capable of blowing teams away can be put down to another abstract word he used post-match in Madrid: ‘brave’.

Tuchel talked in the last international break of ‘unlocking the next level’, and taking ‘calculated risks’ with a ‘man-to-man’ press in the opposition half.

Under Southgate, and certainly in the cowardly retreat against Argentina in the summer, England showed little bravery either with the ball or without it and frequently showed too much respect to those big nations.

Too safe with the ball, too afraid to give it away, and too fearful to try to win it back in case you leave yourself open.

That appears to be changing, too. There was a moment at the start of the second half when Bellingham tried a risky through-ball to Rogers, which failed to find its man, instead of another simple ball out wide.

It handed Spain possession cheaply. But England didn’t care because they just pounced again. Spain couldn’t deal with it. In the first half, Spain completed just 84 per cent of their passes in their own half – a place where they are usually able to knock it about at will – their lowest completion rate according to Opta since the 2010 World Cup. They didn’t have a shot on target until the penalty.

England’s defence has long been seen as the weak spot and, under Southgate, it felt as though he always would rather his attacking talents not be too frivolous for fear of exposing it.

Thomas Tuchel and Kane direct England's players to keep on the front foot during the win over Spain

Tuchel is doing the opposite. England’s expected goals soared from 1.7 per game under Southgate from the 2022 World Cup to the end of his reign, to 2.2 under Tuchel’s until this summer’s tournament. Since then, it’s jumped again to 2.8 but at the cost of what they are conceding. In his early days, England coughed up fewer good chances than under Southgate but since the World Cup has more than doubled.

He will want to get that down, of course, but when you are creating so much – and have an array of top finishers to see them off – how much will that matter to Tuchel?

Even he’s getting braver. His decision to take off Gordon for Konsa and chuck as many defenders on during England’s shrinking against Argentina looked a decision that would forever haunt Tuchel’s tenure.

Against Spain, Kane made way but Tuchel ended the game with striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin on the pitch. Against Spain, he held his nerve.

#1420. DeepMind’s ultra-powerful AI for genome mapping wows scientists

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

In 2024, researchers found a new driver of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD): it was a gene called ETS2 that is overactive in immune cells owing to a DNA variant that predisposes people to the condition1. This variant had previously confounded researchers because it lies in a ‘gene desert’ nowhere near protein-coding sequences.

That discovery had involved gene-editing and other sophisticated molecular-biology techniques, and it identified potential new IBD treatments. Now, researchers at Google DeepMind in London have replicated aspects of the finding using an artificial-intelligence model, and they have done this without lifting a pipette. Their model is called AlphaGenome 2.

“They’ve managed to figure out the answer in 30 minutes, and it took us a year and a half of experiments,” says James Lee, an immunologist and geneticist at the Francis Crick Institute in London, who led the 2024 study. “It’s reassuring from our perspective.”

The AlphaGenome 2 model, which was announced today, is an update to an AI tool that predicts the molecular effects that ‘non-coding’ DNA sequences have, such as on the expression of other genes. These sequences comprise 98% of the human genome, but they are among the hardest to decipher. The latest model makes these predictions in hundreds of mouse and human cell types.

Two months ago, Google DeepMind released the AlphaGenome Atlas: these were predictions for every possible single-letter DNA change to the human genome — a total of nine billion variants.

These and other predictions were made with a tool called AlphaGenome 1 and came with a major caveat: they did not specify the precise kind of cell — be it antibody-making B cells or pancreatic β-cells — in which a variant was likely to act. “Having something that cannot predict cell-type specificity is a bit of a problem, which is why it hasn’t been hugely useful for us,” says Lee.

But researchers know that many non-coding DNA sequences — including the variant that Lee’s team mapped, which is part of a sequence called a gene enhancer — tend to be active in specific types of cell.

“If you want to understand variants associated with genetic diseases, then you have to ask yourself what are the cell types that are affected,” says Žiga Avsec, a DeepMind researcher who leads the AlphaGenome team.

To develop an AI model that could decipher variant effects in diverse cells, Avsec’s team trained AlphaGenome 2 on single-cell gene activity and other measurements made in more than 100 million cells, across 68 tissues. AlphaGenome 1, by contrast, was fed data collected in ‘bulk’ samples of heterogeneous cells.

The result is a richer, more fine-grained representation of the differences between cells, says Adam Gayoso, a Google DeepMind scientist and co-author of a preprint describing the model on the company’s website.

AlphaGenome 2 also isn’t limited to making predictions in the 637 types of human cell and 311 kinds of mouse cell it was trained on. Researchers can provide the model with new single-cell gene-activity data — such as those from cells in a disease state — and generate gene-variant predictions. This could help researchers to identify variants underlying disease more quickly, says Gayoso.

#1419. The cheats prosper: Man City thrash 10-man Liverpool

Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

This is a team who can stir the blood, surf the emotion and triumph against the odds more than any other; who have a proud history of doing so. Who feel the injustice at its most acute and could feed off that.

In the end Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the season. Their first under Andoni Iraola. And comprehensively so. It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

There was another sense of injustice. Up until the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, Liverpool were the better side. Especially as they attacked the Kop in the second half, drawing saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma, and began to build the kind of momentum that has, over the years, appeared to suck the ball into the net.

Ryan Gravenberch is OFF 🟥 https://t.co/IVIHNzqw6k

The midfielder’s first yellow card looked harsh. His second, for a foul on substitute Jérémy Doku was less so (but still not clear-cut) and it meant Liverpool had to play the final third of the game with 10 men. Instead of weaponising that; they wilted and the fans directed their frustration at referee Chris Kavanagh, believing he was lenient towards City.

This is not a slight on Iraola, but it is hard to imagine Jürgen Klopp not riding that wave of emotion more effectively and wringing more out of the available players. Turning to the fans; imploring them; cajoling them.

Instead it was City making the statement with an extraordinary power play as they scored three times in 13 minutes, inspired by Doku, whose cameo made him man of the match. That City could hold the winger back, on the bench, only to introduce him with such devastating effect again pointed to their phenomenal strength in depth.

They are again three points clear at the top, with six wins from six games, ahead of champions Arsenal and there is a frightening awesomeness about them at present that will make the Premier League shudder. For several reasons. What if they run away with it this season before being sanctioned, probably sometime in the spring? Where will that leave the competition?

In the face of City’s power and the adversity of losing Gravenberch, Liverpool simply could not cope. They were already depleted – without Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Cody Gakpo – and needed some of their other big signings to respond.

But this was not a good day for Bradley Barcola or Florian Wirtz, in particular, and it felt telling that the latter was withdrawn soon after Erling Haaland opened the scoring. He could, in fact, have also been sent off after catching Elliot Anderson late. The German’s contribution was once more woefully negligible; worryingly marginal. Enzo Maresca hailed Manchester City’s ability to “make our own noise” after their emphatic 3-0 win at Liverpool.

“It was not easy for the players after the last two, three weeks, but they dealt with it very well,” Maresca, the head coach, said. “I said during the week we need to learn to deal with the outside noise because of the situation, because that will be there. But we have to make our own noise.

“Zero-three at Anfield away is a great result, for sure. I think all the organisation needs a win like this. It’s good for all [of] the club.”

Maresca said City will have to get used to such hostile occasions, with Liverpool fans making clear their anger over the judgment, and added: “All the away games are going to be with noise.”

Maresca confirmed that chief executive Ferran Soriano and director of football Hugo Viana had travelled on the team bus to Anfield in a sign of unity.

“Ferran was there, Hugo was there. We were all together,” Maresca said. “For the importance of the game, Liverpool away, Anfield away. It’s good to be together.”

The Italian claimed that despite the verdict, and the attention and uncertainty as to what will happen next, it had not affected his squad.

“The players just focus on the football. They are not thinking about the future,” he said. “It’s how we learn to deal with the noise. It’s our duty to make noise and to do that we win games. You cannot imagine how happy I am. Hopefully I am going to speak about this situation when we are going to win the appeal.”

The Liverpool boss told BBC MOTD: “I think the first part is that we played two different games. One until the red card, and then after. For 60 minutes, the players were very good. The second game from the red card was where City were better than us.

“The first yellow card was just a kick in the toe. It was nothing. It was a normal foul. It was the moment when we were pushing more. The momentum was coming for us and the atmosphere in the stadium was so nice. We conceded very little in the first half. We did a really good job. The second half, we were translating into chances.

“You learn a lot in games like today. I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It’s a loss and we didn’t get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot.”
